summary.en: Find the reason a design resists change and apply the relevant SOLID principle.
summary.bn: ডিজাইন বদলাতে কোথায় সমস্যা হয় তা খুঁজে প্রাসঙ্গিক SOLID নীতি প্রয়োগ করো।

notes: SOLID principles are design guidance independent of Java version; these examples target Java 17.

sections.title: Find the change that makes a design difficult
Use five questions during a change
Compare a specific design problem with its repair
Describe inputs, results and side effects
Avoid replacing one difficulty with unnecessary machinery
Principles do not depend on a new Java feature
Choose the smallest boundary that solves the observed problem

examples.title: SRP: separate arithmetic from receipt text
examples.explanationHtml: MixedBill combines arithmetic and presentation decisions. Bill and ReceiptText give those independently changing policies separate homes.

examples.title: OCP: move fare variants out of a central branch
examples.explanationHtml: The central branch needs edits for new fare kinds. A Fare implementation extends the supported policy family while the caller keeps amount(distance).

examples.title: LSP: express the capability actually required
examples.explanationHtml: Box promises writable storage, but FixedBox breaks that promise. Archive implements only Reader. The invalid write is explained without invoking it.

examples.title: ISP: stop demanding unused operations
examples.explanationHtml: The wide interface forces scan clients to acknowledge printing. ScannerDevice gives them exactly the capability they require.

examples.title: DIP: supply a message destination
examples.explanationHtml: FixedNotifier constructs a concrete destination. Notifier depends on Sink and receives a destination, so policy and delivery can vary independently.

practice.title: Extend discount policies
practice.statementHtml: Read kind (0 no discount, 1 half, 2 subtract ten) and price (0..10000). Create a Discount interface and three implementations. A Checkout receives Discount and delegates total(price). Print the nonnegative total.
hints: Keep the policy selection outside Checkout.

practice.title: Inject a recording sink
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..20) then n marks (0..100). MarkService receives a Sink with record(int). SumSink stores total and CountSink counts records. Run each mark through two services and print sum and count separated by one space.
hints: The service knows record(), not a concrete storage type.

practice.title: Diagnose a stronger precondition
practice.statementHtml: Account.withdraw accepts any positive amount up to balance. A subclass rejects amounts below 500. Identify the violated principle and repair the abstraction.
practice.answerHtml: This violates LSP by strengthening a precondition. A caller using the Account contract may legally withdraw 100 and unexpectedly fail. Preserve the parent’s withdrawal rule, or model the restricted product through a different contract that states the minimum amount.
hints: Compare what callers are allowed to ask.

practice.title: Separate two reasons to change
practice.statementHtml: One Result class calculates grades and sends email. Identify independent change sources and propose classes.
practice.answerHtml: GradePolicy changes when academic rules change. ResultNotifier changes when delivery requirements change. Keep grade computation separate from message delivery, and have a small application operation coordinate them. This follows SRP without requiring one class for every line of code.
hints: Name who requests each kind of change.

practice.title: Distinguish DIP from injection
practice.statementHtml: A constructor receives a concrete ConsoleSink. Does that alone establish dependency inversion?
practice.answerHtml: No. Constructor injection controls who supplies the object, but the consumer still depends on a concrete class. DIP asks policy and details to depend on a suitable abstraction. Accept a narrow Sink interface when alternate destinations are useful.
hints: Look at the declared dependency type.

quiz.prompt: Which injected calculator does Service use?
quiz.explanation: The service delegates to the supplied DoubleValue policy.

quiz.prompt: Does separating formatting change the numeric total?
quiz.explanation: The arithmetic returns fourteen and the separate formatter prefixes the currency label.
options: BDT 14
BDT 9
BDT 27

quiz.prompt: Can two services share the same recording sink?
quiz.explanation: Both services hold the same sink reference, so two calls increment one shared count.

quiz.prompt: What does SRP ask you to separate?
quiz.explanation: A responsibility is a coherent policy or change source, not a line count.
options: Responsibilities with different reasons to change
Every two methods
Every field into its own class

quiz.prompt: What is an OCP extension boundary?
quiz.explanation: Existing consumers can remain stable while new implementations extend supported behaviour.
options: A ban on all future edits
A stable contract with replaceable implementations
A class with only public fields

quiz.explanation: A stronger precondition breaks callers that rely on the parent contract.
options: A subtype computes faster
A subtype adds a private helper
A subtype rejects input the parent promises to accept

quiz.explanation: ISP groups operations around client needs, not a universal method-count rule.
options: Clients depend on the small capability they need
Every device implements a giant interface
All interfaces have exactly one method

quiz.prompt: What dependency direction does DIP encourage?
quiz.explanation: The abstraction describes what the policy needs and decouples it from delivery or storage details.
options: Business policy constructs every concrete adapter
Policy and details depend on abstractions
Interfaces depend on every application class

quiz.prompt: Must every class receive an interface wrapper?
quiz.explanation: Unnecessary abstractions make small stable designs harder to follow.
options: Yes, SOLID mandates it
Only utility classes need interfaces
No, introduce a boundary where variation or isolation helps

quiz.prompt: What evidence best supports an exam answer naming LSP?
quiz.explanation: A behavioural counterexample explains the violation rather than merely naming the principle.
options: A concrete legal parent call that the child breaks
The child has fewer fields
The child file is longer

quiz.prompt: What does constructor injection primarily decide?
quiz.explanation: The dependency may still be concrete; DIP and injection are related but distinct.
options: Whether the dependency is automatically abstract
Who supplies a dependency instance
Whether the class becomes immutable

quiz.explanation: Weakening the promised result makes previously valid callers unsafe.
options: Returning a more specific valid result
Removing internal duplicate work
Returning null where the parent promises a non-null result

keyPoints.en: SRP separates policies that change for different reasons.
keyPoints.bn: ভিন্ন কারণে বদলায় এমন নীতি SRP আলাদা করে।

keyPoints.en: OCP needs a stable boundary for useful extensions.
keyPoints.bn: উপযোগী সম্প্রসারণের জন্য OCP-তে স্থিতিশীল চুক্তি দরকার।

keyPoints.en: LSP preserves the behavioural promises of the parent.
keyPoints.bn: LSP প্যারেন্টের আচরণগত প্রতিশ্রুতি বজায় রাখে।

keyPoints.en: ISP follows client needs rather than arbitrary interface sizes.
keyPoints.bn: ISP ইন্টারফেসের আকার নয়, ক্লায়েন্টের প্রয়োজন অনুসরণ করে।

keyPoints.en: DIP directs both policy and details toward abstractions.
keyPoints.bn: DIP নীতি ও বাস্তবায়ন দুটোকেই অ্যাবস্ট্রাকশনের ওপর নির্ভর করতে বলে।

examQuestions.question: Explain all five SOLID principles using the marks-reporting domain.
examQuestions.answerHtml: SRP separates grading from delivery. OCP adds grade policies behind a stable contract. LSP requires new policies to accept the documented marks and return valid grades. ISP separates reading results from editing them. DIP makes reporting depend on a destination interface rather than constructing one specific sender.

examQuestions.question: A read-only file subclass inherits a promise that write always succeeds. Diagnose and redesign.
examQuestions.answerHtml: LSP is broken when the subclass rejects a promised operation. Separate Readable and Writable capabilities. A read-only implementation supplies Readable; clients needing writes require Writable. This also applies ISP by preventing read clients from depending on write operations.

examQuestions.question: How should an interview answer balance SOLID and unnecessary abstraction?
examQuestions.answerHtml: Identify the actual change pressure and one failing interaction. Choose the smallest useful separation, explain the contract, and mention the cost of extra types and indirection. Do not invent extension points with no expected variation or testing benefit.
